title: My ex texted me after ten years
author: Storytime
hook: My only ex-girlfriend texted me for the first time in ten years. She said, I have something that belongs to you. I need to give it back.
story: Emma and I dated for four years at university. We broke up badly, and we haven't spoken in ten years. Last week, two days after I got engaged, a message popped up. Hi. I heard the news. Congratulations. I have something that belongs to you. Can we meet? My heart dropped. My fiancee, Lucy, said, go. Just tell me everything after. So I met Emma at a little café. She looked nervous. She slid a small velvet box across the table. Inside was a ring. My mum's ring. My mum passed away eleven years ago. I spent years thinking that ring was lost. Emma said, your mum gave it to me, a month before she died. She made me promise not to tell you. Then she handed me an envelope. In my mum's handwriting, it said, give this back when he's found the one who makes him laugh the way you used to. Emma said, I heard Lucy makes you laugh. So here it is. Then she paid for my coffee and left. I haven't told Lucy about the letter yet. Part two?
caption: my mum planned this eleven years ago 💍 #storytime
sound: a soft, bittersweet piano at very low volume
why: An ex reaching out after years is trending, viewers expect drama, the mum's ring twist is deeply emotional, and the letter sets up a natural part two.

title: Two proposals at the same restaurant
author: Storytime
hook: When I told my best friend I got engaged, she burst into tears. Not happy tears. Then she told me why.
story: Last Saturday, my boyfriend Ben proposed to me at our favorite Italian restaurant. Candles, violin, the whole thing. I said yes, obviously. The next morning, I called my best friend Kayla first. Before my mom. Before anyone. I screamed, I'm engaged! There was a long silence. Then she started crying. Not happy crying. Ugly crying. I panicked. I thought she hated Ben. I thought she was in love with him. She finally said, it's not you. It's the restaurant. Kayla had been planning to propose to her girlfriend, Jess, at that exact restaurant. Same table. That same night. She had a ring in her pocket. She was sitting in the corner booth when Ben got down on one knee. Kayla saw me crying, saw the whole restaurant clapping, and put the ring back in her pocket. She didn't want to steal my moment. Jess still has no idea. Kayla said she'll find another night. But I can't stop thinking about it. Ben suggested we invite them back to the restaurant, same violinist, and let Kayla have her moment. Should we do it?
caption: she put the ring back in her pocket for me 💍 #storytime
sound: a romantic violin melody at very low volume
why: Best friend reactions to engagements are trending, the ugly crying misleads viewers, the hidden second proposal is a sweet twist, and the redo question invites supportive comments.

title: Everyone fought over the newspaper gift
author: Storytime
hook: At our office gift exchange, everyone fought over the ugliest gift. A box wrapped in old newspaper. I know why.
story: Every December, our office does a white elephant gift exchange. You can steal gifts. This year, there was one box nobody wanted. Wrapped in old newspaper and tape. Our new intern, Priya, got stuck with it. She opened it. Inside was a twenty dollar bill and a note. Whoever ends up with this at the end gets an extra week of paid vacation. Signed by our CEO. The room exploded. It got stolen four times. The last person to steal it was my manager, Greg. He laughed and waved it in Priya's face. Priya looked crushed. She hasn't been home to see her family in two years. Then it was my turn. I was the last one. I stole it from Greg. Then I walked over and handed it to Priya. Greg said I wasted it, and that the CEO meant it as a game. This morning, the CEO emailed the whole company. He said, the game was never about the box. Greg and I both have a meeting with him tomorrow. Should I be worried?
caption: the ugliest gift was the best one 🎁 #storytime
sound: a playful holiday jingle with a sly twist at very low volume
why: Office gift exchange season is starting, the ugly newspaper box is a fun hook, giving it to the intern is satisfying, and the CEO meeting cliffhanger drives comments.
